world.title: Nepal sends aid by helicopter as Gorkha flood leaves five missing
world.summary: Nepalese rescue teams reached flood-hit villages along the Budhi Gandaki River on Monday, delivering food and relief supplies and evacuating residents and tourists after Sunday’s flash flood in Gorkha district. Five people were reported missing, and no deaths had been confirmed. Authorities said 95 people, including ni
world.content: Nepalese rescue teams reached flood-hit villages along the Budhi Gandaki River on Monday, delivering food and relief supplies and evacuating residents and tourists after Sunday’s flash flood in Gorkha district. Five people were reported missing, and no deaths had been confirmed. Authorities said 95 people, including nine foreign nationals, had been taken to nearby towns. The flood damaged or destroyed homes, bridges and infrastructure at three hydropower construction sites. With bridges and road links cut in the mountainous area, helicopters are carrying supplies to villages cut off by road, while trucks deliver food, tents and medicine to accessible locations. Officials suspect a landslide blocked the river near Chumchure before water broke through, but they are still assessing the damage. October is a busy period for visitors to the region’s trekking routes, and Nepal’s disaster authority has warned communities to remain alert as rescue and evacuation work continues.

world.title: Polish police arrest suspect in alleged plot against Tusk and defence minister
world.summary: Polish police arrested a man suspected of planning an attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz after security officials said they received credible information about a possible assassination attempt. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński confirmed the arrest on Sunday, Oct. 11,
world.content: Polish police arrested a man suspected of planning an attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz after security officials said they received credible information about a possible assassination attempt. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński confirmed the arrest on Sunday, Oct. 11, and Tusk thanked police for acting quickly. Authorities have not publicly disclosed the suspect’s identity or the planned method of attack. The State Protection Service, which guards ministers, passed information about the threat to police. An email prompted an emergency meeting involving security services, police and Interior Ministry representatives. Special services spokesman Jacek Dobrzyński said officials judged the likelihood that the threats would be carried out to be high. Police continued their investigation and searched the suspect’s home, Interior Ministry spokeswoman Karolina Gałecka said. The arrest followed a week of school attacks in central Poland that killed one person and wounded several others, including children.
world.image_alt: Polish police arrest suspect in alleged plot against Tusk and defence minister

world.title: French center-left picks Raphaël Glucksmann for 2027 presidential race
world.summary: Raphaël Glucksmann won the French center-left’s presidential primary on Oct. 11 with 66.17% of the vote, securing the backing of the Socialist Party and its allies for the 2027 election. Organizers said 120,787 people voted. Glucksmann, a European Parliament member and leader of Place Publique, has called for a left-wi
world.content: Raphaël Glucksmann won the French center-left’s presidential primary on Oct. 11 with 66.17% of the vote, securing the backing of the Socialist Party and its allies for the 2027 election. Organizers said 120,787 people voted. Glucksmann, a European Parliament member and leader of Place Publique, has called for a left-wing campaign against the far right and opposed an alliance with Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s France Unbowed party. A recent Ifop poll cited by Politico put Mélenchon at 14% to 17% and Glucksmann at 11%. Glucksmann is a strong supporter of Ukraine and a critic of China. Voting began Friday, and organizers extended it to Sunday evening after a cyberattack slowed the online process. They said the attack did not compromise the recorded votes. The first round of France’s presidential election is scheduled for April 18, 2027.
world.image_alt: French center-left picks Raphaël Glucksmann for 2027 presidential race

world.title: Iran rejects US response to seven terms for reopening Hormuz
world.summary: Iran said Sunday that the United States’ response to its seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz was insufficient and that Tehran would not reply again until Washington clarified unresolved points. Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, said the United States had accepted some conditions but left others uncl
world.content: Iran said Sunday that the United States’ response to its seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz was insufficient and that Tehran would not reply again until Washington clarified unresolved points. Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, said the United States had accepted some conditions but left others unclear. The two sides have exchanged proposals through regional mediators. The conditions include ending the US naval blockade of Iranian ports and restrictions on Iranian oil exports. Iran has offered to restore normal passage within seven days if its terms are met. Washington has rejected Tehran’s proposal for Iran and Oman to jointly manage the waterway and says ships should have free passage under international law. The dispute follows the outbreak of war in February and the collapse of a June US-Iran memorandum on navigation. An unidentified projectile hit a tanker leaving the strait on Sunday. Its crew was safe, and no environmental impact was reported.
world.image_alt: Iran rejects US response to seven terms for reopening Hormuz

world.title: Pope Leo XIV schedules lung nodule surgery, expects weeklong recovery
world.summary: Pope Leo XIV, 71, said on Oct. 11 that he will undergo surgery in Rome in the coming days to remove a small, localized nodule found during recent medical checks. The Vatican expects his recovery to take about a week. Leo said doctors found the nodule at a very early stage and advised removal. The procedure is expected
world.content: Pope Leo XIV, 71, said on Oct. 11 that he will undergo surgery in Rome in the coming days to remove a small, localized nodule found during recent medical checks. The Vatican expects his recovery to take about a week. Leo said doctors found the nodule at a very early stage and advised removal. The procedure is expected to take place at Gemelli Hospital, though the Vatican has not announced the exact date. The finding does not establish that the nodule is cancerous. Specialists say lung nodules are often benign, but benign and cancerous nodules can look similar on imaging; removal can provide a definitive diagnosis. Leo has no previously known health problems and is physically active, according to reports. His recovery could keep him from attending the Wednesday closing Mass of a Vatican family-ministry conference. Leo said he still plans to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from Nov. 6 to 17, but it remains unclear whether surgery will affect that itinerary.
world.image_alt: Pope Leo XIV schedules lung nodule surgery, expects weeklong recovery

world.title: UK prime minister says Russia interfered in 2016 Brexit vote
world.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham says Russia interfered in the 2016 Brexit referendum and that advisers gave him a “clear answer” when he asked after taking office in July. In podcast excerpts released Sunday, Burnham did not explain how Russia intervened, provide evidence or say whether any interference affected th
world.content: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham says Russia interfered in the 2016 Brexit referendum and that advisers gave him a “clear answer” when he asked after taking office in July. In podcast excerpts released Sunday, Burnham did not explain how Russia intervened, provide evidence or say whether any interference affected the result. The claim is the first public acknowledgment of Russian interference in the referendum by a British prime minister. A 2020 report by Parliament’s Intelligence and Security Committee criticized the government for failing to fully assess the possible impact of Russian state media and online “troll” accounts; it did not establish whether Russia had interfered in the Brexit vote. Former Prime Minister Boris Johnson said in 2020 that there was no evidence of Russian interference, while Moscow has repeatedly denied meddling in other countries’ elections. Burnham said he raised the issue with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz at a meeting in Berlin and wants voters in France and Germany to be alert to foreign efforts to disrupt politics. He said Merz had described the far-right Alternative for Germany party as linked to Russia and, he believed, funded by it. Burnham also said Russian disinformation was circulating in German politics.
world.image_alt: UK prime minister says Russia interfered in 2016 Brexit vote

world.title: Delhi shuts six metro stations as opposition plans election protest march
world.summary: Delhi authorities closed six metro stations and imposed traffic restrictions on Monday, Oct. 12, as leaders of the opposition Congress party prepared to march to the Supreme Court to protest voter-roll changes and demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. Chief Justice Surya Kant declined Congress
world.content: Delhi authorities closed six metro stations and imposed traffic restrictions on Monday, Oct. 12, as leaders of the opposition Congress party prepared to march to the Supreme Court to protest voter-roll changes and demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. Chief Justice Surya Kant declined Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s request for a meeting, saying the disputed issues should be raised in legal proceedings because related cases are already before the court. The voter verification exercise, which began last year, removed more than 130 million names from electoral lists. Opposition parties say the deletions may disproportionately affect Muslim and other minority voters and benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party. The Election Commission and BJP deny manipulation, saying the exercise removes ineligible or duplicate entries. The Supreme Court held a special hearing on Sunday after police detained demonstrators and restricted access to central Delhi. It directed authorities to avoid illegal detentions and disruptions to internet access, and said lawyers and journalists should be able to work without obstruction. The Cockroach Janta Party said it would ask Delhi police for a date for a peaceful protest and could call for another protest if police did not provide one within 24 hours.
world.image_alt: Delhi shuts six metro stations as opposition plans election protest march

world.title: Sudanese rights group says suspected Egyptian strike killed 72 miners
world.summary: A Sudanese rights group said airstrikes hit an artisanal gold-mining site near the disputed Sudan-Egypt border on Saturday, killing at least 72 people. It accused Egypt’s air force, but the allegation and death toll have not been independently verified. Egypt has not commented on the reported attack. The remote site li
world.content: A Sudanese rights group said airstrikes hit an artisanal gold-mining site near the disputed Sudan-Egypt border on Saturday, killing at least 72 people. It accused Egypt’s air force, but the allegation and death toll have not been independently verified. Egypt has not commented on the reported attack. The remote site lies in a border region claimed by both countries, and survivors described people fleeing after repeated strikes. The attack was the second reported strike on the Jabal al-Uqaydat mining area this year. A similar attack in June reportedly killed 23 workers; Egypt’s military said at the time that it had conducted a large-scale operation against illegal mining within Egyptian territory. Artisanal gold mining has expanded during Sudan’s war, which began in April 2023 and has killed more than 200,000 people, according to reports cited by the rights group and news organizations. Gold also finances armed groups. Chatham House estimates that as much as 60% of Sudan’s unofficial gold exports go to Egypt. Sudan Doctors Network warned that the casualty toll could rise because seriously injured people struggle to reach medical care.
world.image_alt: Sudanese rights group says suspected Egyptian strike killed 72 miners

Rising costs are increasingly pricing out would-be buyers, Bloomberg reported. Yahoo Finance also reported an affordability gap in South Bend, Indiana.
business.content: Home prices and mortgage costs are making housing less affordable across the Midwest, a region often viewed as a refuge from the U.S. housing squeeze. Rising costs are increasingly pricing out would-be buyers, Bloomberg reported. Yahoo Finance also reported an affordability gap in South Bend, Indiana.

business.title: Volkswagen chief backs EU rules tying support to European production
business.summary: Volkswagen chief executive Oliver Blume called for closer cooperation between France and Germany to strengthen Europe’s car industry against Chinese rivals and backed EU proposals that reward production and investment in Europe. Speaking in Paris before the motor show, he said companies investing and developing in Euro
business.content: Volkswagen chief executive Oliver Blume called for closer cooperation between France and Germany to strengthen Europe’s car industry against Chinese rivals and backed EU proposals that reward production and investment in Europe. Speaking in Paris before the motor show, he said companies investing and developing in Europe should benefit, and competitors selling there should create jobs and economic value there. The proposed EU Industrial Accelerator Act would link some subsidies and public procurement to products with substantial EU-based manufacturing and materials. Blume cited high energy costs, weak demand from consumers facing inflation and intensified competition from China. Volkswagen is undertaking what he described as the biggest transformation in its history, including plans to cut as many as 100,000 jobs. French President Emmanuel Macron also advocates a European preference for public support, but France and Germany have not agreed on an approach. The Élysée denied a reported deal linking stricter local-production rules to a relaxation of the EU’s 2035 emissions target. The Paris Motor Show is scheduled to open to the public from October 13 to 18.
business.image_alt: Volkswagen chief backs EU rules tying support to European production

business.title: Retirement planning depends on spending, income and household costs
business.summary: Reports published Oct. 11 examined the financial and personal trade-offs of leaving work at 65, with The Washington Post noting that the calculations vary widely by household. Fortune focused on retirees’ concerns about whether Social Security will remain available, though the supplied description of its report include
business.content: Reports published Oct. 11 examined the financial and personal trade-offs of leaving work at 65, with The Washington Post noting that the calculations vary widely by household. Fortune focused on retirees’ concerns about whether Social Security will remain available, though the supplied description of its report includes no specific benefit forecasts or policy proposals. Certified financial planner Kevin Lum said retirees may be more financially secure than they feel if they spend modestly, have no debt, have guaranteed income or health coverage, and can adjust discretionary spending. He cautioned that fixed withdrawal rules such as the 4% rule may be difficult to follow as expenses change; flexible plans allow spending to vary with market conditions.

business.title: Asian shares waver as oil retreats and earnings loom
business.summary: Asian shares were mixed on Monday, Oct. 12, as investors weighed the start of earnings season against shifting oil-supply expectations. Brent crude fell 1.6% to $103.01 a barrel and U.S. crude dropped 1.9% to $90.11; South Korea’s benchmark fell 2.2%, while MSCI’s broad Asia-Pacific index excluding Japan slipped 0.3%.
business.content: Asian shares were mixed on Monday, Oct. 12, as investors weighed the start of earnings season against shifting oil-supply expectations. Brent crude fell 1.6% to $103.01 a barrel and U.S. crude dropped 1.9% to $90.11; South Korea’s benchmark fell 2.2%, while MSCI’s broad Asia-Pacific index excluding Japan slipped 0.3%. Trading was thin, with Japan’s markets closed and U.S. markets on a partial holiday. Oil prices retreated after President Donald Trump announced an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia and proposed that Russia increase diesel exports. Neither side had confirmed the ceasefire, and senators from both parties questioned whether the export proposal was legal. Major U.S. banks are due to begin reporting earnings on Tuesday, and TSMC is expected to post a sixth consecutive quarter of record earnings on Thursday.
business.image_alt: Asian shares waver as oil retreats and earnings loom

business.title: AI compute shortage pushes rivals to share capacity and accept costly deals
business.summary: AI companies are scrambling for computing power as demand for capacity to train and run advanced models outstrips supply, prompting competitors and investors to secure capacity together. Anthropic and Elon Musk’s companies negotiated a computing agreement, while cloud providers increasingly require multiyear contracts
business.content: AI companies are scrambling for computing power as demand for capacity to train and run advanced models outstrips supply, prompting competitors and investors to secure capacity together. Anthropic and Elon Musk’s companies negotiated a computing agreement, while cloud providers increasingly require multiyear contracts and large upfront payments. The shortage is raising costs and making delivery schedules uncertain: rental rates for Nvidia chips under one-year contracts rose 60% year over year, and some providers seek deposits of up to 30% of the contract value. Cohere co-founder Nick Frosst said some announced data-center projects have been canceled or built at a smaller scale than promised; a delay at a partner data center cost startup Arcee a deal. Separately, U.S. data centers use Chinese-made equipment and U.S. companies rely on Chinese AI, The Washington Post reported.
business.image_alt: AI compute shortage pushes rivals to share capacity and accept costly deals

business.title: AI investment boosts trade as financial and inequality risks rise
business.summary: Investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure is driving a sharp rise in trade in chips and servers, but analysts warn that spending may outpace profits and that gains are concentrated in a small group of countries. The World Trade Organization raised its 2026 forecast for merchandise trade growth to 3.9%; AI-re
business.content: Investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure is driving a sharp rise in trade in chips and servers, but analysts warn that spending may outpace profits and that gains are concentrated in a small group of countries. The World Trade Organization raised its 2026 forecast for merchandise trade growth to 3.9%; AI-related products accounted for 47% of trade growth in the first half of the year, with their trade value up 67% from the same period in 2025. Spending on data centers, chips and AI models has prompted concerns about financial losses if expected earnings fail to materialize. The IMF has warned that countries lacking digital infrastructure, capital and skilled workers risk falling behind. Experts cited by El País expect AI to change the nature of work more than the total number of jobs, while warning that it could widen wage inequality. Black Lake chief executive Zhou Yuxiang says some Chinese factories are adopting AI agents without first completing traditional digitization.
business.image_alt: AI investment boosts trade as financial and inequality risks rise

business.title: IFS warns UK chancellor faces £35bn Budget gap before October 28
business.summary: The Institute for Fiscal Studies warned Chancellor John Healey that meeting the government’s spending ambitions could require up to £35bn in additional funding or cuts elsewhere ahead of his first Budget on 28 October. Higher inflation linked to the Iran war is eroding the purchasing power of departmental budgets, whil
business.content: The Institute for Fiscal Studies warned Chancellor John Healey that meeting the government’s spending ambitions could require up to £35bn in additional funding or cuts elsewhere ahead of his first Budget on 28 October. Higher inflation linked to the Iran war is eroding the purchasing power of departmental budgets, while Healey aims to raise defence spending to 3% of national income by 2030 and increase health spending. The IFS said Healey must set out credible spending plans rather than defer hard choices to a later spending review. Options include tax rises, benefit cuts or reduced public services. Higher borrowing costs could add about £10bn to borrowing in 2029-30, while the IFS estimates the government’s fiscal-rule buffer may shrink to around £20bn. The Treasury declined to comment on speculation. The Office for Budget Responsibility is due to publish an updated forecast alongside the Budget.
business.image_alt: IFS warns UK chancellor faces £35bn Budget gap before October 28

business.title: Legal experts question DOJ antitrust probe of five TV networks
business.summary: The Justice Department sent civil investigative demands to ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC as it examines whether their brief suspension of White House television pool coverage violated federal antitrust law. The department says coordinated boycotts by commercial competitors can violate the Sherman Act and is seeking m
business.content: The Justice Department sent civil investigative demands to ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC as it examines whether their brief suspension of White House television pool coverage violated federal antitrust law. The department says coordinated boycotts by commercial competitors can violate the Sherman Act and is seeking material related to the networks’ pool decisions. Legal experts quoted by The Washington Post questioned whether the networks’ conduct constitutes an illegal boycott, while Cornell law professor Michael Dorf said the legal review would turn on whether their actions were reasonable. The Justice Department’s investigation is separate from the press-access case: a federal judge extended an order temporarily restoring credentials for CNN, MS NOW and Politico through Tuesday, when he is expected to issue another decision.
business.image_alt: Legal experts question DOJ antitrust probe of five TV networks

science.title: UK forecasters say aurora could be visible through Tuesday
science.summary: Forecasters said the aurora could remain visible in parts of the UK on Sunday and Monday, with the Met Office forecasting possible sightings under clear skies through Tuesday, Oct. 13. Scotland and northern England were among the areas with the best viewing prospects, while cloud was expected to spread into western Sco
science.content: Forecasters said the aurora could remain visible in parts of the UK on Sunday and Monday, with the Met Office forecasting possible sightings under clear skies through Tuesday, Oct. 13. Scotland and northern England were among the areas with the best viewing prospects, while cloud was expected to spread into western Scotland. The forecast follows a weekend display reported from Scotland, Wales and northern England. WalesOnline said two glancing coronal mass ejections, followed by a high-speed stream from a coronal hole, could continue to enhance auroral activity. The Met Office forecast sightings where skies are clear, and STV meteorologist Sean Batty said cloud cover could limit views in western Scotland.
science.image_alt: UK forecasters say aurora could be visible through Tuesday

science.title: Olive oil before carbohydrates blunts blood sugar rise in mice, study finds
science.summary: Giving mice olive oil 15 minutes before glucose reduced the initial blood sugar rise and slowed stomach emptying compared with giving oil afterward, a study found. The researchers also observed early increases in glucagon, GIP and GLP-1, including in mice with type 2 diabetes and severe insulin deficiency. The mouse re
science.content: Giving mice olive oil 15 minutes before glucose reduced the initial blood sugar rise and slowed stomach emptying compared with giving oil afterward, a study found. The researchers also observed early increases in glucagon, GIP and GLP-1, including in mice with type 2 diabetes and severe insulin deficiency. The mouse results do not establish whether giving olive oil before glucose has the same effect in people. The researchers said clinical studies are needed to test whether the response can help regulate blood sugar in humans.
science.image_alt: Olive oil before carbohydrates blunts blood sugar rise in mice, study finds

science.title: Studies link gut metabolite to Alzheimer’s changes, test rapamycin
science.summary: A study of nearly 1,200 older adults found that higher blood levels of imidazole propionate, a metabolite produced by some gut bacteria, were associated with poorer cognitive scores and faster decline. Experiments in mice used to model Alzheimer’s disease also found that the metabolite worsened brain pathology. The hum
science.content: A study of nearly 1,200 older adults found that higher blood levels of imidazole propionate, a metabolite produced by some gut bacteria, were associated with poorer cognitive scores and faster decline. Experiments in mice used to model Alzheimer’s disease also found that the metabolite worsened brain pathology. The human observations do not show that lowering the metabolite prevents dementia. Separately, a four-week pilot study gave low-dose rapamycin to healthy adults aged 45 to 65. Brain blood flow improved only among participants carrying the APOE4 Alzheimer’s risk variant. The study did not test whether the change prevents Alzheimer’s or preserves memory over time.
science.image_alt: Studies link gut metabolite to Alzheimer’s changes, test rapamycin

science.title: NASA selects GIMLI mission to probe suspected lunar cave
science.summary: NASA has selected the GIMLI project to investigate a suspected underground cave at the Moon’s Marius pit using radar and seismic tests. The project aims to determine whether the feature could provide natural shelter for future astronauts. The target is described as a possible lava tube and a candidate site for a future
science.content: NASA has selected the GIMLI project to investigate a suspected underground cave at the Moon’s Marius pit using radar and seismic tests. The project aims to determine whether the feature could provide natural shelter for future astronauts. The target is described as a possible lava tube and a candidate site for a future lunar base, but its structure and suitability remain unknown.
science.image_alt: NASA selects GIMLI mission to probe suspected lunar cave

science.title: Indonesia releases eight orangutans rescued from fires into protected Borneo forest
science.summary: Indonesian authorities and the YIARI wildlife rehabilitation foundation released eight orangutans into Batu Nyambu Protected Forest in West Kalimantan on Friday after wildfires threatened the animals’ habitat on Borneo. The group includes three mothers with their offspring and two adolescent males. The 23,000-hectare r
science.content: Indonesian authorities and the YIARI wildlife rehabilitation foundation released eight orangutans into Batu Nyambu Protected Forest in West Kalimantan on Friday after wildfires threatened the animals’ habitat on Borneo. The group includes three mothers with their offspring and two adolescent males. The 23,000-hectare reserve was chosen for its food and water sources and connections to other forest areas. Authorities and YIARI rescued 46 orangutans affected by fires between August and October 9. El Niño conditions and land-clearing practices have been cited as factors in Indonesia’s intensified fires this year. The Indonesian government has warned that the blazes, which have hit Sumatra and Borneo, could continue until November.
science.image_alt: Indonesia releases eight orangutans rescued from fires into protected Borneo forest

science.title: NASA features 2010 photo of IceCube detector installation in Antarctica
science.summary: NASA’s Oct. 11 astronomy feature presented a 2010 photograph of one of the last IceCube detector strings being lowered into a borehole near the South Pole. The feature described the installation as part of an observatory built to detect high-energy neutrinos from powerful cosmic processes. The photograph shows how astr
science.content: NASA’s Oct. 11 astronomy feature presented a 2010 photograph of one of the last IceCube detector strings being lowered into a borehole near the South Pole. The feature described the installation as part of an observatory built to detect high-energy neutrinos from powerful cosmic processes. The photograph shows how astronomers installed IceCube: They lowered a string of light detectors into a hole melted in the ice, which later refroze around the detectors. NASA said the detectors register blue light from secondary particles created when neutrinos collide with molecules in the surrounding ice.
science.image_alt: NASA features 2010 photo of IceCube detector installation in Antarctica

science.title: Pacific El Niño sets September sea-temperature records as event intensifies
science.summary: The developing 2026 El Niño pushed sea-surface temperatures in the Pacific’s Niño 3.4 reference region to a record 29.70°C in September, while average sea temperatures outside polar waters reached a September record of 21.05°C, Copernicus reported. The episode is expected to strengthen and peak in December, but Coperni
science.content: The developing 2026 El Niño pushed sea-surface temperatures in the Pacific’s Niño 3.4 reference region to a record 29.70°C in September, while average sea temperatures outside polar waters reached a September record of 21.05°C, Copernicus reported. The episode is expected to strengthen and peak in December, but Copernicus cautioned that the record readings alone do not establish it as the strongest El Niño ever. Scientists must separate the pattern’s effects from long-term ocean warming. September was the second-warmest month on record globally, at 1.63°C above preindustrial levels. It was the second consecutive month above 1.5°C, a threshold assessed over long-term averages rather than individual months. El Niño shifts rainfall patterns, increasing the likelihood of wetter conditions in some regions and drought in others. Its effects on Europe are less direct, and it cannot determine a winter forecast on its own.
science.image_alt: Pacific El Niño sets September sea-temperature records as event intensifies

sports.title: UCLA stays unbeaten with 17-15 win over Oregon
sports.summary: No. 21 UCLA beat No. 13 Oregon 17-15 at Autzen Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 10, to remain unbeaten and hand the Ducks their second loss of the season. UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava left with a lower-leg injury, but backup Ty Dieffenbach threw a fourth-quarter touchdown pass to Wayne Knight. Oregon rallied late but faile
sports.content: No. 21 UCLA beat No. 13 Oregon 17-15 at Autzen Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 10, to remain unbeaten and hand the Ducks their second loss of the season. UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava left with a lower-leg injury, but backup Ty Dieffenbach threw a fourth-quarter touchdown pass to Wayne Knight. Oregon rallied late but failed to convert a two-point try that would have tied the game. Oregon fell out of the AP Top 25 for the first time in four years. UCLA is 5-0 and hosts Wisconsin next Saturday, while Oregon (3-2) hosts Nebraska.
sports.image_alt: UCLA stays unbeaten with 17-15 win over Oregon

sports.title: China’s Zheng Qinwen wins historic China Open title over Andreeva
sports.summary: China’s Zheng Qinwen beat fourth-seeded Mirra Andreeva 7-5, 6-4 in Beijing on Sunday to become the first Chinese woman to win the China Open and claim her first WTA 1000 title. Zheng, 24, entered as a wildcard ranked 54th and ended a title drought dating to Tokyo in October 2024. The Olympic champion saved three set po
sports.content: China’s Zheng Qinwen beat fourth-seeded Mirra Andreeva 7-5, 6-4 in Beijing on Sunday to become the first Chinese woman to win the China Open and claim her first WTA 1000 title. Zheng, 24, entered as a wildcard ranked 54th and ended a title drought dating to Tokyo in October 2024. The Olympic champion saved three set points in the opener, then won 11 consecutive points to take the set; she broke Andreeva at 4-4 in the second and sealed the win with an ace. The victory followed a difficult return from elbow surgery in 2025, which had contributed to a steep slide in her ranking; she fell as low as 160th this season. Zheng said she felt she had forgotten how to compete after returning from injury and described finding her “fire again” after many losses. The win is expected to lift her to 23rd in the rankings, while Andreeva, 19, is projected to rise to a career-high third despite the defeat. Zheng was due to play in Wuhan this week but withdrew on Monday, citing fatigue after the Beijing tournament.
sports.image_alt: China’s Zheng Qinwen wins historic China Open title over Andreeva

sports.title: Crystal Palace rally past Forest 3-1 to spoil Glasner’s return
sports.summary: Crystal Palace came from behind to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday, October 11, spoiling former manager Oliver Glasner’s return. Dan Ndoye put Forest ahead in the third minute, but Daichi Kamada equalised before Jefferson Lerma’s stoppage-time goal and Yeremy Pino’s 59th-minute finish completed th
sports.content: Crystal Palace came from behind to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday, October 11, spoiling former manager Oliver Glasner’s return. Dan Ndoye put Forest ahead in the third minute, but Daichi Kamada equalised before Jefferson Lerma’s stoppage-time goal and Yeremy Pino’s 59th-minute finish completed the comeback. Forest controlled much of the opening half and created several clear chances, but Palace goalkeeper Walter Benítez kept them at bay. The result gave Palace manager Pierre Sage his first home Premier League win and moved the club to 12th with seven points; Forest fell to 14th on five. Glasner, who took charge of Forest after leaving Palace, where he led the club to trophies, said he had “no rational explanation” for the defeat despite calling it his side’s best performance of the season. Palace’s next listed fixture is away to Lyon in the Europa League on Thursday, October 15.
sports.image_alt: Crystal Palace rally past Forest 3-1 to spoil Glasner’s return

sports.title: Hull salvage Everton draw as Belloumi preserves unbeaten home run
sports.summary: Hull City and Everton drew 2-2 at the MKM Stadium on Sunday, with Mohamed Belloumi’s 74th-minute equaliser earning the newly promoted hosts a point. Joe Gelhardt put Hull ahead three minutes after half-time. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall equalised for Everton in the 55th minute, and Thierno Barry gave the visitors a 2-1 lead i
sports.content: Hull City and Everton drew 2-2 at the MKM Stadium on Sunday, with Mohamed Belloumi’s 74th-minute equaliser earning the newly promoted hosts a point. Joe Gelhardt put Hull ahead three minutes after half-time. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall equalised for Everton in the 55th minute, and Thierno Barry gave the visitors a 2-1 lead in the 68th minute. The result extended Hull’s unbeaten home record since their return to the Premier League and left Everton unbeaten after six league matches. Hull had nine points and Everton had 10. Everton manager David Moyes said his side’s performance fell well below the expected level and that he would not accept ownership or transfer uncertainty as an excuse.

sports.content: Eliud Kipchoge won the Melbourne Marathon in 2:09:10 on Sunday, October 11, breaking the course record by two seconds for his first marathon victory since Berlin in 2023. The 41-year-old Kenyan pulled away from Australian challengers in the closing stages, then slowed to wave to spectators as he finished inside the Melbourne Cricket Ground. The course also included part of the Albert Park Formula One circuit. Australian Thomas Do Canto finished second in 2:10:35. Kipchoge said he believes he can still compete with younger runners and called the Melbourne crowd and course a highlight. Melbourne was the third stop on Kipchoge’s two-year plan to run a marathon on all seven continents, including Antarctica. He has said the world tour will raise money for his foundation, which supports education, environmental sustainability and health.

sports.content: After Manchester United’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham, manager Michael Carrick said his team must become “more streetwise” and defend leads with greater resolve. Goalkeeper Senne Lammens said the players must learn quickly from the late equaliser. United have six points from six league matches, their poorest start at this stage in 40 years. Luke Shaw was seen limping after the match, though an injury had not been confirmed. Carrick said striker Benjamin Sesko’s problem was still being assessed and surgery was one possibility under consideration. Former players and pundits called for tactical changes to United’s midfield, while Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi said his side’s response showed the fight he wants them to sustain. United travel to Atlético Madrid on Tuesday before returning to league action away to Leeds five days later.

sports.content: The Washington Commanders and New York Giants tied 27-27 at Northwest Stadium on Sunday after Washington let the overtime clock expire without attempting a potential game-winning field goal. With 12 seconds left, the Commanders had the ball at New York’s 24-yard line and no timeouts. Quarterback Jayden Daniels was tackled in bounds, and Washington could not line up to spike the ball before time ran out. The Giants had erased a 27-13 fourth-quarter deficit with two Jameis Winston touchdown passes, then lost possession in overtime when Daron Payne forced Cam Skattebo to fumble. Daniels returned after dislocating his left elbow in Week 2 and finished with 199 passing yards, 103 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns. He and coach Dan Quinn accepted responsibility for the closing sequence, with Quinn saying the team should have stopped the clock earlier. New York remains atop the NFC East at 3-1-1, while Washington is 1-3-1. The Giants host New Orleans on Oct. 18, and the Commanders visit San Francisco on Oct. 19.

sports.content: The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 2-1 in Milwaukee on Oct. 11 to take a 1-0 lead in the National League Championship Series. Brice Turang tied the game with a solo homer off Tarik Skubal in the fourth inning. Rookie Luis Lara put Milwaukee ahead with a fifth-inning single after Garrett Mitchell walked and Cooper Pratt advanced him to second with a sacrifice. Jacob Misiorowski allowed one run in 4⅓ innings, throwing 94 pitches before Milwaukee turned to four relievers, who held Los Angeles to two hits over the final 4⅔ innings. The win ended Milwaukee’s seven-game postseason losing streak against the Dodgers, including a four-game sweep in last year’s NLCS. Game 2 is scheduled for Monday, Oct. 12, in Milwaukee, with Yoshinobu Yamamoto starting for Los Angeles and Logan Henderson for the Brewers. The Dodgers are pursuing a third consecutive World Series title, while Milwaukee is seeking its first.
